blocks.text: Organizing your Chrome workspace for ad management

The secret to a productive media buying setup is isolation. You likely manage accounts for different clients, each with their own set of login credentials and tracking pixels. If you mix these in one Chrome window, you risk data leakage or accidental account switching. Create a dedicated Chrome profile for each major client or brand. Go to the profile icon in the top right corner and select Add. This keeps cookies, history, and bookmarks separate for every account.
Using tab groups to track campaigns

Once you have your profiles, use tab groups to manage your daily tasks. Right click any tab and choose Add tab to new group. Name the group after the campaign or the specific task, such as Daily Performance or Creative Review. This prevents the dreaded tab overflow where you lose track of which window contains your Google Ads dashboard and which holds your client report. If you have many tabs, you can collapse the group by clicking its name to save screen space.
Keyboard shortcuts to speed up your analysis

Your mouse is a bottleneck. To move faster, memorize the core Chrome shortcuts. Press ⌘ + T for a new tab and ⌘ + L to jump immediately to the address bar. If you need to jump between tabs, use ⌘ + Option + Right Arrow or ⌘ + Option + Left Arrow. These small movements add up when you are checking performance metrics across five different platforms every hour.

Lazur acts as a bridge between your thoughts and your browser. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask questions about anything on your screen. If you are looking at a complex dashboard and cannot find the export button, ask Lazur where it is. It will circle the element for you. When you need to draft a quick email to a client about a budget shift, hold fn to dictate the text directly into your email client. It handles formatting and keeps your hands on the keyboard.

Media buyers often deal with tracking pixels and third party scripts that can slow down your browser. If a specific ad platform dashboard starts behaving strangely, you do not need to clear your entire browser cache. Navigate to Settings > Privacy and security > Site settings > View permissions and data stored across sites. Search for the specific domain and clear data only for that site. This fixes bugs without logging you out of every other tool you use.
Researching new ad trends with Lazur

When you need to research a new ad format or platform policy, do not spend hours manually opening and closing tabs. Ask Lazur to research the topic. It opens its own private tabs to gather information and returns a summary. This keeps your main browser workspace clean and focused on your active campaigns. It is a simple way to offload the cognitive load of information gathering.

blocks.text: The importance of a clean setup

Your browser is your primary tool. Treat it like a physical desk. If it is cluttered, your work will suffer. Spend five minutes at the end of each day closing unnecessary tabs and organizing your bookmarks. If you find yourself doing the same tasks in Chrome repeatedly, check if you can use a custom shortcut or a snippet to handle them. Lazur can help you remember your custom workflows if you ask it to recall what you did yesterday.

Start by auditing your current Chrome setup. Are you using profiles? Do you have a system for managing your tabs? Once your browser is optimized, introduce Lazur to handle the friction points. Whether it is dictating quick notes during a meeting or asking for help with a specific menu path, the goal is to keep you in your flow state. Your time is valuable. Stop wasting it on manual browser tasks and start focusing on your campaign results.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons in Chrome for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not interact with web pages or click buttons. It can point to where a button is on your screen or guide you through a menu path, but you must perform the actual click.

faq.question: How do I keep client data separate in Chrome?
faq.answer: The best way is to use Chrome profiles. Each profile acts as a completely separate browser instance with its own history, cookies, and bookmarks.

faq.question: Does Lazur store my screen content?
faq.answer: No. Lazur only looks at your screen while you are holding the shortcut key. The screenshot is sent to the AI provider to answer your query and is not stored or used for training.

faq.question: What is the best way to manage many tabs?
faq.answer: Use Chrome's native tab grouping feature. Right click a tab to create a group and color code it by client or project.

faq.question: How can I fix a website that will not load?
faq.answer: First, try clearing the site data for that specific domain in Chrome settings. If that fails, check your extensions to see if one is blocking the site.
